main_text.p: stit ad angulos rectos in duplici fiffura horizon-tis, vt tanto rectius circumduci poffit, prout vfus poftulat.

Sicut autem duæ funt fiffuræ in ipfo horizonte, ita tertia fiffura eft in parua quadam columna erecta in medio ftatumine siue bafi, extra quam fiffuram conftitutus meridianus nullum habet rectum in alueo fi-tum.

3. Horizon & Meridianus in cœlo terraque varii sunt & mutabiles pro locorum mutatione, vt fupra docuimus: sed in globis materialibus hisce vterque circulus aliter fieri non potuit, quam fimplex, conftans & inuariabilis, quia globus cœlum repræfentat abfolute.

4. Per Meridianum atque adeo etiam per totum globi corpus transfixus eft ftylus siue æneus siue ferreus, qui exacte medium globi perftranfit, & Diameter globi siue axis mundi appellatur, circa quem tota fphæra ita neceffario circumuoluitur, vt rota circa fuum axem.

5. Huius ftyli siue axis duæ funt extremitates ex ipfo circulo meridionali partibus recta oppo-fitis emergentes, quæ dicuntur Poli, vnus nempe Septentrionalis, alter vero Meridionalis: quorum ille si globus recte ad noftrum vfum fit conftitu-tus, supra horizontem in globo eleuatur: hic vero semper infra horizontem deprimitur ad i-pfum globi ftatumen.

6. Meridianus circulus diuifus eft in 4. qua-drantes, quorum quadrantum duæ funt notæ, 1. numerus denarius nouies repetitus, siue nume-rus nonagenarius: altera nota funt areolæ infculp-tæ in ipfum æs, quarum quælibet vnum gradum defignat, ita vt fi omnes gradus simul computes, inuen-

page.notes: Page is a right-hand page from a bound volume; left edge is the gutter and shadowed. Some ink is faint at the line ends, notably "inuen-" at the bottom, which continues onto the next page. Page number 172 read from the head line. Word "Meridianus" and "Diameter" are as printed.
